pairs.question: Qui sunt ii, qui rem publicam occupauere?
pairs.answer: Homines sceleratissimi, cruentis manibus, immani auaritia, nocentissimi et idem superbissimi, quibus fides decus pietas, postremo honesta atque inhonesta omnia quaestui sunt.
pairs.derivation: In Memmius' contio (ch.31) the speaker poses an anticipated question and answers it himself. Dropped the leading connective 'At' (framing) and normalized capitalization on the question. Answer is the immediate self-answer; cut at the first full stop after 'quaestui sunt.', before the elaboration 'Pars eorum occidisse tribunos plebis...' which goes on to detail their crimes.

pairs.question: Quid igitur censes?
pairs.answer: Vindicandum in eos, qui hosti prodidere rem publicam, non manu neque vi, quod magis vos fecisse quam illis accidisse indignum est, verum quaestionibus et indicio ipsius Iugurthae.
pairs.derivation: Memmius' speech (ch.31) explicitly stages the question, attributing it to a hypothetical interlocutor: 'Dicet aliquis "quid igitur censes?"'. Dropped the speech-frame 'Dicet aliquis' (narration of who asks) and the surrounding quotation marks; normalized capitalization. Answer cut at the first full stop after 'indicio ipsius Iugurthae.', before the conditional elaboration 'Qui si dediticius est...'.
